descriptor.scene: The same plain door as it will hang someday: framed on the cream museum wall, a soft spotlight pooling on it, the velvet rope in place, the floor polished and empty of people. On the wall beside the frame, a small brass plaque with designed lettering that is fully legible and reads exactly "THE AGENTS" in two clean words, spelled letter for letter T-H-E A-G-E-N-T-S, and nothing else. The scene is imagined, serene, a little too tidy, the way the past always looks once it is finished. Keep the bottom right calm. The door leaf has EXACTLY FOUR recessed panels in TWO rows and no more: a top row of two small square panels, and below it a single row of two tall rectangular panels that reach nearly to the floor with only a plain flat rail beneath them. There is NO third row of panels at the bottom of the door.
negatives: any lettering other than the quoted plaque string
lettering on the door face itself
a six-panel colonial door, a third row of panels at the bottom of the door leaf
descriptor._caption: Someday this door will hang in the hall like the others, lit and labeled and roped off, and people will say nobody could have missed it. That is how every open door looks, after.
